title: Intermittent credential rotation idempotency bug causing transient tenant authorization failures
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Production incidents reported by two Dedicated customers (AcmePay and NovaRetail) where API requests were intermittently returning 403s immediately after a scheduled credential rotation. Symptoms were short (~10-45s) windows of tenant-scoped authorization failure tied to token refresh flows and autoscaling events. This ticket tracks investigation, emergency mitigation, patch, QA, rollout, and postmortem actions.

root_cause: During credential rotation we allowed concurrent refresh requests to proceed without global coordination. When a refresh coincided with an autoscale-induced node drain and our alias-binding backfill job, the apikey->tenant mapping in the fastpath cache could be transiently replaced with a stale alias. The request path accepts the freshly rotated token but looks up tenant roles via the fastpath cache which had intermediate state (alias tombstone) leading to 403 decisions. Two contributing factors: (1) no refresh idempotency/lock, (2) cache eviction/backfill window and leader election race in token-service during scale events.
mitigation_and_fix: Hotfix: introduce a lightweight distributed per-apikey refresh lock (etcd-backed lease) to serialize concurrent refreshes and make rotation idempotent. Delay fastpath cache eviction by 5s after an alias swap and add atomic compare-and-set on alias updates. Permanent fix: (a) leader election stabilization improvements in token-service, (b) stronger apikey alias CAS semantics, (c) telemetry to surface alias swap durations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In dedicated staging, schedule apikey rotation for test-tenant A
2) While rotation runs, trigger scale-down of one serving node in the same pool to force token-service leader handoff
3) Fire a burst of client-refresh requests (simulate SDK retries) to produce concurrent refresh attempts
4) Observe 403s on subset of requests for 10-60s and verify fastpath cache shows transient alias tombstone entries
5) Reproduce deterministically by introducing a 100-200ms sleep in alias-backfill job to widen the race window.
qa_plan: Unit tests for refresh lock semantics and alias CAS
Integration test: rotation + node drain scenario automated in e2e harness (ci/rotations/rotation_drain_test)
Chaos test: run 100 rotations with randomized delays while autoscaling a dedicated pool for 24h in staging
Load test: simulate SDK with exponential backoff to ensure no elevated 429s or deadlocks
rollout_plan: Canary in us-west-2 dedicated pool (5% of traffic) for 1 hour
If no error signal, expand to all dedicated pools over 2 hours
Apply same change to Private package and schedule customer-side upgrade notes
Monitor Datadog alerts for authorization-403, alias-swap-latency, and token-service leader-churn
postmortem_actions: Add telemetry to track alias swap durations and frequency
Run a one-time audit to detect apikeys that experienced >1 swap in 60s window and notify owners
Backfill documentation for rotation operational playbook and include rollback steps
Schedule reliability spike for token-service leader election performance improvements in Q2 roadmap
customer_comm: 03/10: Initial ack and temporary mitigation applied; engineering team investigating root cause
03/11: Hotfix deployed; asked customers to validate and observed no recurrences

notes: Observed SDKs that aggressively retry without jitter increased the likelihood of concurrent refresh collisions
Consider adding guidance in SDKs to use single-flight refresh for apikey rotation events
Edge case: Private on-prem customers with slower control-plane connectivity may experience longer alias swap windows; include recommended retry/backoff settings in upgrade notes
